title: BLS Employment Projections: National Employment Matrix, Veterinary services (NAICS 541940), 2025 and projected 2035

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the fetched document.

publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Projections program
source_type: Government statistical table (industry-by-occupation employment matrix with projections)
reliability: Government statistical page; BLS is a neutral statistical agency, but figures are model-based projections. Release date is not shown on the page text read; it reports 2025 employment and a 2035 projection.
findings: Veterinary services (NAICS 541940) total employment is 473.6 thousand in 2025, projected 511.8 thousand in 2035 (+38.2 thousand, +8.1%).

Veterinarians are 75.5 thousand (15.9%) of industry employment in 2025, veterinary technologists and technicians 116.6 thousand (24.6%), and veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers 113.6 thousand (24.0%).
Office and administrative support occupations total 105.9 thousand (22.4% of industry employment) in 2025, projected 106.9 thousand in 2035 (+1.0 thousand, +1.0%); its share falls to 20.9%.

Within office and administrative support in 2025: receptionists and information clerks 55.6 thousand (projected 56.2), customer service representatives 18.5 thousand (projected 18.3), first-line supervisors of office and administrative workers 11.8 thousand, bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerks 2.7 thousand.
Projected 2025-2035 growth is 9.9% for veterinarians, technicians and assistants, versus 1.0% for office and administrative support overall.
limitations: Industry-wide table for all veterinary services employers; it does not distinguish independent practices from corporate-owned or hospital groups, and does not show practice size.
Employment counts and projections only: no hours, tasks or workload, so it does not measure administrative burden or unmet staffing need.
Rounded to 0.1 thousand; small occupations are suppressed. Release date and methodology notes were not read.
Table rows were parsed from the page HTML; the occupation-level figures were not independently recomputed.
